reply_text:
I found one candidate for 2019. On Facebook's first-quarter 2019 earnings call (24 April 2019), Zuckerberg talked about the AI systems that find harmful posts before anyone reports them. He said they likely wouldn't reach 99% in every category "in the next six months or a year." He hoped they would reach "90-plus percent on most of these categories within the next couple of years." The quote comes from Facebook's own investor-relations transcript (a PDF), which I opened. One thing to judge: "a couple of years" sits close to the "a few years" wording your rules treat as undated. I kept it because the same answer also names six months and a year.

**Pages I opened that had nothing to list:**
- **Conversation with Yuval Noah Harari (April 2019, Facebook's transcript PDF):** a lot about AI, but nothing with a date or a timeframe.
- **Conversation with Jonathan Zittrain at Harvard (February 2019, Facebook's transcript PDF):** no dated AI forecast.
- **ABC interview with George Stephanopoulos (April 2019):** only describes what the AI systems already did, for example removing 99% of ISIS and Al-Qaeda content before anyone sees it.
- **Fourth-quarter 2018 earnings call (held 30 January 2019):** describes current AI work only.
- **Third-quarter 2019 earnings call (30 October 2019):** he said he didn't "foresee any time in the near future that AI is going to make it so that this -- the cost comes down." That has no date and is about review costs, not AGI, so I left it out.

**Not checked:** the October 2019 Georgetown speech, the October 2019 Libra hearing, the second-quarter 2019 call and his 2019 Facebook posts. All 6 page openings were used and 10 of the 12 searches. The first fixed search ran once; my code crashed while printing it and I read the saved result rather than running it again.
